operations.content: LLM Prompt KV-Cache Optimization (Stable Prefix Pattern): Structure agent prompts with stable prefix (identity, tools, output format, examples) before dynamic content ({{variables}}, {{code}}, {{playbook_bullets}}). LLMs cache inference computations (KV-cache) for stable prefixes, reducing latency 30-50% and cost proportionally. Move frequently-changing content to END of prompt. Pattern: <identity>→<tools>→<format>→{{dynamic}}. Enables provider-level caching (Anthropic prompt caching, OpenAI cached completions).

# ❌ INEFFICIENT - dynamic content early
You are {{role}}. Here's the code: {{code}}.
Your tools: Read, Write, Edit.
Output JSON format: {...}

# ✅ EFFICIENT - stable prefix, dynamic at end
You are an expert developer.
Your tools: Read, Write, Edit.
Output JSON format: {...}

Now analyze this code:
{{code}}
```

operations.content: Quantitative Thresholds Over Vague Adjectives: Replace subjective adjectives with concrete numerical thresholds in specifications, validation rules, and agent instructions. Use ≥0.85 instead of 'very similar', score 8-10/10 instead of 'good quality', <3 iterations instead of 'few retries'. Eliminates interpretation variance across LLM runs and enables objective validation. Pattern: identify adjective → define measurement axis → specify threshold with units.

N-Dimensional Quality Model with Explicit Criteria: For complex validation (code review, content quality, system design), define N-dimensional evaluation model with explicit What/How/Pass-Fail per dimension. Structure: Dimension name, What it measures, How to assess (method/metric), Pass threshold, Fail indicator. Forces systematic review, prevents dimension skipping. Minimum 5 dimensions for production code, 3 for documentation. Example dimensions: Correctness, Security, Performance, Testability, Maintainability.

...
```

operations.new_content: Bidirectional Template Synchronization for CLI Tools: When developing CLI tools that distribute templates via package managers (pip install, npm install), maintain bidirectional sync between development templates (.claude/) and distribution templates (src/templates/). Pattern: (1) Dedicated verification subtask in workflows, (2) Automated check script (./scripts/check-template-sync.sh using diff -q), (3) Git pre-commit hook preventing commits with drift, (4) Explicit sync steps in developer workflow documentation. Critical because users running 'mapify init' receive templates from packaged src/templates/, NOT .claude/ development directory. Template drift causes production users to get outdated patterns while development benefits from improvements. Evidence: Zero drift issues across 8 agent templates + 6 command templates after implementing comprehensive sync workflow (ST-008 prompt optimization).
operations.new_code_example:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# scripts/check-template-sync.sh - Comprehensive verification
echo "Checking template synchronization..."

OUT_OF_SYNC=0
for agent in task-decomposer actor monitor predictor evaluator reflector curator; do
  source=".claude/agents/${agent}.md"
  target="src/mapify_cli/templates/agents/${agent}.md"
  
  if [ -f "$source" ] && [ -f "$target" ]; then
    if ! diff -q "$source" "$target" > /dev/null; then
      echo "❌ OUT OF SYNC: agents/${agent}.md"
      echo "   Run: cp $source $target"
      OUT_OF_SYNC=1
    else
      echo "✅ IN SYNC: agents/${agent}.md"
    fi
  else
    echo "⚠️  MISSING: agents/${agent}.md"
    OUT_OF_SYNC=1
  fi
done

exit $OUT_OF_SYNC
```

operations.content: Cross-Agent Schema Consistency via Canonical Definitions: When multiple agents evaluate using shared models (dimensional quality, scoring rubrics, data schemas), create .claude/schemas/ with canonical JSON Schema definitions that all agents reference. Pattern: (1) Define schema once in .claude/schemas/evaluation_dimensions.json, (2) Agents import via {{schema}} template variable, (3) Validation gate checks schema matches across agent templates, (4) Schema versioning (v1, v2) for breaking changes. Prevents dimensional model drift (Monitor uses 6D model, Evaluator uses 7D model causing inconsistency). Especially critical for multi-agent workflows where agents must agree on evaluation criteria.
